purpose: Verified publisher bibliographic records, not extra critical-source credit.

works.title: The Republic
works.description: A philosophical dialogue about justice, education, knowledge and the relationship between a person and a political community.

edition.translation_notes: Standard English edition of the dialogue, introduced by Melissa Lane. Original composition year remains approximate and is not assigned a false exact date.

works.title: The Souls of Black Folk
works.description: A book uniting sociological argument, historical reflection and personal experience to examine the color line and Black life in America.

edition.translation_notes: Publisher identifies all fourteen essays as the book, with introduction by Randall Kenan and afterword by Cheryl Townsend Gilkes. Rank the authored book as a whole, not its individual chapters.

works.title: On the Origin of Species
works.description: A sustained argument about variation and natural selection, presented through comparisons and accumulated observations. Read as a foundational scientific work in its historical context.

edition.translation_notes: Anniversary edition with introduction and scholarly references by William Bynum, cover by Damien Hirst. Standard book edition, not a modern adaptation; no claim that it replaces current biological scholarship.

works.title: Silent Spring
works.description: A work of environmental nonfiction examining pesticide use and its consequences through scientific reporting and public argument.

edition.translation_notes: Paperback metadata follows the New Zealand publisher record for this ISBN. This is the standard book, not the separate Penguin short-extract edition. Current science and policy require newer sources.

works.title: An Enquiry concerning Human Understanding
works.description: A connected philosophical investigation of experience, belief, causal reasoning and the limits of human knowledge.

edition.translation_notes: Edited by Lorne Falkenstein. Publisher contents list all twelve sections, plus contextual responses by Campbell, Reid, Beattie and Kant. The 312-page extent includes this apparatus.

works.title: On Liberty
works.description: A book-length argument about individuality, discussion and the limits of social authority. Its universal language must also be read alongside its exclusions.

edition.translation_notes: Edited by Edward Alexander. Publisher identifies the text of On Liberty followed by contextual appendices, chronology and bibliography; the 294-page extent includes the apparatus. Harriet Taylor’s intellectual contribution is acknowledged without inventing a separate title-page coauthor.
